subject: Post-demo: clarification on DPA roles, subprocessors, residency & breach notice
messages:
From: Lily Chen <lily.chen@medsecure.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medsecure.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Redwood demo — DPA details and breach notification

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo this morning — the team found Redwood's latency guarantees and routing options compelling. Before we take this to legal and security for an evaluate-and-approve pass, a few clarifying items came up that I want to capture in writing so our counsel can triage: 

1) Controller vs Processor: We need explicit language on the DPA that confirms MedSecure is the Controller and Redwood Inference is the Processor. Are there any processing activities where Redwood would be considered a Controller (e.g., model improvement or telemetry)?

2) Subprocessors: Please provide a current list of subprocessors and your typical onboarding/notification cadence. If you use cloud providers (e.g., GCP/AWS regions), we'd like to know which subprocessors have access to decrypted content, if any.

3) Data residency: We heard there are hosted US and EU regions and an on-prem/private option. Can you confirm which product tiers support EU residency specifically for tokenized and raw request logs?

4) Logging & retention: What logs are kept by default (request/response, metadata, error traces, usage metrics) and what are the default retention windows? Is custom retention on a per-customer basis possible?

5) Breach notification: What is Redwood's timeline and escalation process if a security incident affects customer data? We need a clear window (hours) and an outline of what evidence you will provide (audit logs, scope, remediation steps).

If it helps, we can share a shortlist of the clauses that matter most to our counsel. For next steps, can you share any DPA template/redline and SOC2 evidence we can attach to our review?

Thanks — appreciate a concise response so we can move to legal review.

Lily
Lily Chen
Sr. Security & Privacy Program Manager
MedSecure Health
[phone redacted]
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lily Chen <lily.chen@medsecure.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood demo — DPA details and breach notification

Hi Lily — great to meet you earlier. Thanks for the clear list; below are high-level answers. I'm copying Ben (sales lead) and Stephanie (security/compliance) to add evidence and any finer points.

1) Controller / Processor: MedSecure is the Controller; Redwood acts as a Processor for all inference and storage activities under the hosted and dedicated products. We do not use customer request data to train models unless explicitly agreed and contractually permitted — no training-by-default. 

2) Subprocessors: We use a limited set of subprocessors (cloud providers, monitoring, logging vendors). Ben/Stephanie: attaching current inventory and a short explanation of which subprocessors handle decrypted data. We will include the last notification date and onboarding checklist.

3) Data residency: Hosted product supports US- and EU-region tenancy; EU residency (logs and control-plane metadata) is available on our Dedicated and Private tiers for customers requiring strict residency. We can provide an addendum that pins log residency.

4) Logging & retention: Default retention is 90 days for request/response metadata and 30 days for application-level traces. Raw request/response bodies are configurable and can be excluded or retained per contract. We offer custom retention on Enterprise and Dedicated plans.

5) Breach notification: Redwood's standard is to notify customers as soon as we have confirmed customer impact and to provide an initial incident brief within 72 hours. We run an internal triage that collects scope, affected resources, and a remediation plan; we can provide audit logs and a playbook for investigations. Stephanie — please share the playbook and SOC2 evidence. Ben — please attach the subprocessor CSV and the sample DPA redline.

I'll consolidate and send an external-facing packet to Lily once I have everything.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com
[attachment: meeting-recording-2026-07-14.mp4 (video/mp4)]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood demo — DPA details and breach notification

Mina / Steph — attaching the files Lily asked for. Quick notes inline:

- Attachment: subprocessor_inventory_2026-07.csv — current list with roles, jurisdiction, and whether the subprocessor has access to plaintext. Cloud VM hosts (GCP us-west1, AWS eu-west-1) do not have Redwood access to customer plaintext except for short-lived runtime keys; only our logging vendor (LogStream Inc.) processes aggregated metadata, not full request bodies.

- Attachment: SOC2_report_redwood_2025.pdf — redacted SOC2 Type II report; includes control descriptions relevant to access control and change management.

- Attachment: sample_privacy_addendum_redlined.docx — our standard DPA with optional clauses highlighted (residency pinning, extended retention, subprocessor notification terms).

On the "controller" point — the DPA explicitly states customer control over data categories and purpose limitations. We never classify ourselves as a Controller for customer-provided prompts.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood demo — DPA details and breach notification

Adding a couple of technical clarifications for Lily (feel free to paste this into the external packet):

- Logging retention: default 90 days for request metadata and 30 days for full trace/debug logs. For customers on Dedicated or Private we can extend retention or disable specific logging categories. Retention controls are enforceable via contract, and we provide a retention report on request.

- Residency: Hosted EU region ensures control-plane and storage within EU IaaS boundaries; however, certain ephemeral operational telemetry (service health metrics) may route through a US-based control plane unless you purchase the Private control plane option. For customers requiring full EU-only processing we recommend Dedicated with EU-region pinning or Private on-prem deployment.

- Breach playbook: we will provide a redacted incident playbook that shows timelines, escalation points, and sample evidence artifacts. Initial customer notification: within 72 hours of confirmed impact; further updates per SLA (24/48-hour cadence) until resolution.

I'm attaching breach_playbook_redwood.pdf and will follow up with a short logging-sample extract that shows fields we can provide on incident.

-Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
